title: Decimal arithmetic: Hive's result types, half up, overflow raises (ANSI) or NULL
verdict: result types borrow scale past 38 digits; `decimal_rescale`: `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO`; overflow: `ERROR` (ANSI) or NULL
description: Result types follow Hive's rules (`DecimalPrecision`): `DECIMAL(10,2) + DECIMAL(10,1)` is `DECIMAL(12,2)`, `*` is `DECIMAL(21,3)` (scale s₁ + s₂), `/` is `DECIMAL(22,13)` (scale max(6, s₁ + p₂ + 1)), `%` is `DECIMAL(10,2)`. Past 38 digits, with `spark.sql.decimalOperations.allowPrecisionLoss` on (the default), the scale is cut to no less than 6: `DECIMAL(38,10) * DECIMAL(38,10)` is `DECIMAL(38,6)`; with it off the scale is kept and the integer digits shrink (`DECIMAL(38,20)`).

A result with more digits than its scale rounds half away from zero (`ROUND_HALF_UP` on `java.math.BigDecimal`): `CAST(0.125 AS DECIMAL(10,2))` is 0.13 and -0.125 gives -0.13; `round` does the same, `bround` rounds half to even. `1.00 / 8` is 0.125000, `2 / 3` 0.666667.

A result past its precision raises `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` under ANSI and is NULL without it (`a + a` for `a` = 10³⁸ - 1). `sum` of `DECIMAL(p,s)` returns `DECIMAL(p + 10, s)` and `avg` `DECIMAL(p + 4, s + 4)`; a decimal `sum` past 38 digits raises under ANSI (`ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` on the codegen path, `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` on the folded one) and is NULL without it. `DECIMAL(39,0)` is refused when the query is analysed.
Negation and `abs` are different: they round to 34 significant digits (SP-1, spark-decimal-negate).
reference: `functions_arithmetic_decimal.yaml` gives the result types (multiply: scale s₁ + s₂, divide: max(6, s₁ + p₂ + 1), precision capped at 38 by borrowing scale) and no rounding; the reference rounds half away from zero (`decimal_rescale`), with `overflow: ERROR`. Decimal division is refused until #27; ST-8 records the open rounding. Spark under ANSI gives the YAML's types, the reference's rounding and its overflow natively.

evidence.note: `CheckOverflowInSum`: NULL or a raise by the eval mode

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `DECIMAL(38,18)` operands: `+` and `-` are `decimal(38,17)`, `*` and `/` `decimal(38,6)` (precision loss allowed, ANSI on)
after `set spark.sql.decimalOperations.allowPrecisionLoss=false`, `DECIMAL(38,18) * DECIMAL(38,18)` is `decimal(38,36)` and `/` `decimal(38,18)`, ANSI off
the same query is NULL, a `decimal(38,1)`, ANSI off
the same is NULL, a `decimal(8,6)`, ANSI off

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
